curatorBrief.title: Adventures in Adding Up to 10
curatorBrief.intent: Welcome first-grade mathematicians to the world of addition within 10. Introduce the concept of putting groups together to find a total, recognizing the mathematical signs (+ and =), and connecting fun visual story scenes directly to addition number sentences.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Combine two groups of real objects to find the total sum up to 10

components.title: Combine Counters on the Ten-Frame
components.intent: Guide students to combine two groups of counters (e.g., red and yellow) onto a single ten-frame to find the total count up to 10 using concrete visual representation.

components.title: Add More Objects to Find the Sum
components.intent: Provide interactive practice where students combine sets of concrete objects (such as apples or stars) and say the total number aloud to reinforce one-to-one counting and cardinality up to 10.

components.title: Choose Ways to Add Objects
components.intent: Engage students in exploring different visual strategies (like drawing objects or counting on a ten-frame) to combine two groups and find sums within 10.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Identify the plus (+) and equals (=) signs in a number sentence

components.title: Exploring Math Signs: Plus and Equals
components.intent: Introduce and define the plus sign (+) as 'putting together or adding' and the equals sign (=) as 'is the same amount as', highlighting each symbol clearly within a number sentence.

components.title: Build Equations with + and =
components.intent: Allow students to place the plus sign and equal sign into blank spaces within addition number sentences, reinforcing the role and position of each symbol.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Explain how a picture story matches an addition equation

components.title: Act Out Addition Story Scenes
components.intent: Show illustrated joining stories (such as frogs joining on a log or birds landing on a branch) and guide students to explain aloud and match the scene to the corresponding addition equation within 10.

components.title: Explain the Picture Story
components.intent: Prompt students with an illustrated addition situation and ask them to explain aloud in their own words how the two parts in the picture make the whole number sentence.

finalAssessment.title: Addition Explorer Checkpoint
finalAssessment.intent: Assess mastery across all three objectives: combining object sets to determine sums within 10, identifying the plus (+) and equals (=) symbols in equations, and matching pictorial joining scenes to their corresponding number sentences.

challenges.hint: Count out three red counters one by one onto the frame.

challenges.instruction: Put 3 counters on the ten frame!

challenges.hint: Fill the top row with 4 counters.
challenges.narration: Great job! Now let's place 4 counters on the frame.
challenges.instruction: Put 4 counters on the ten frame!

challenges.hint: Fill the entire top row completely.
challenges.narration: Can you show me 5 counters on the frame?
challenges.instruction: Put 5 counters on the ten frame!

challenges.hint: Fill the top row of 5 and add 1 more to the bottom row.
challenges.narration: Let's build a total of 6 counters.

challenges.hint: Put 5 on top and 2 on the bottom.
challenges.narration: Now let's place 7 counters on the frame.
challenges.instruction: Put 7 counters on the ten frame!

challenges.hint: Fill the top row and add 3 to the bottom row.
challenges.narration: Let's make a group of 8 counters.
challenges.instruction: Put 8 counters on the ten frame!

challenges.hint: Fill every single space on the ten-frame!
challenges.narration: For our final challenge, fill the entire ten-frame to make 10!
challenges.instruction: Put 10 counters on the ten frame!

data.title: Combine and Count Butterflies
data.description: Combine sets of concrete objects and say the total number aloud to reinforce one-to-one counting and cardinality up to 10.

challenges.instruction: Put three more butterflies on the board. How many altogether?
challenges.hint: Try tapping each butterfly one by one as you count them up to the total.
challenges.narration: Let's add more butterflies to our circle and see how many we have altogether!

challenges.instruction: Put three more butterflies on the board. How many altogether?
challenges.hint: Take your time and touch each butterfly as you count them.
challenges.narration: Let's put a few more butterflies on the board and count the whole group!

challenges.instruction: Put one more butterflies on the board. How many altogether?
challenges.hint: Count carefully from the very first butterfly to the last one in the line.
challenges.narration: Now we are adding even more butterflies to our line. Let's count them all!

challenges.instruction: Put one more butterflies on the board. How many altogether?
challenges.hint: Count the butterflies in each group, then keep going until you reach the end.
challenges.narration: Let's combine these groups of butterflies and see what our grand total is!

challenges.instruction: Put three more butterflies on the board. How many altogether?
challenges.hint: Make sure you count every single butterfly without missing any!
challenges.narration: You've added all the butterflies! Let's do a final count of everything altogether.

data.title: Pick-a-Strategy Addition Adventure!
data.description: Discover and apply fun visual methods like drawing objects and ten-frames to combine groups and find sums within 10.

challenges.instruction: Let's solve this by counting back! Start from the bigger number and count down.
strategySteps: Find the bigger number in our subtraction problem and say it out loud.
Use your fingers to show the smaller number we need to take away.
Count backwards on your fingers for each one you take away, and see what number you land on!

strategyDescriptions.counting-back: Start at the bigger number and count down.

challenges.instruction: Let\'s solve this addition problem by counting on! Remember to start from the bigger number.
strategySteps: Identify which of our numbers is the bigger one: 6 or 3.
Start your voice at that bigger number and get ready to count.
Count forward by the value of the smaller number, one step at a time.
Look at the last number you said. That is your final answer!

strategyDescriptions.counting-on: Start at the bigger number and count up.

challenges.instruction: Let's use tally marks to solve this! Draw tally groups for each number and count them all together.
strategySteps: Draw 5 tally marks for the first number.
Draw 5 more tally marks right next to them.
Count all the tally marks together to find the total.

strategyDescriptions.tally-marks: Draw a tally mark for each, then count them all.

challenges.instruction: Let's use our super doubles power to solve this! When we add the exact same number twice, we call it a double.
strategySteps: Look at the two numbers you are adding together. Are they the exact same number?
Think of your favorite doubles fact song or chant for this number.
Put the two equal groups together in your mind to find the total.

strategyDescriptions.doubles: Use a doubles fact you already know.

data.objectiveText: Identify the plus (+) and equals (=) signs in a number sentence

diagram.description: A clear math number sentence '3 + 2 = 5' showing the plus sign, equals sign, and the full number sentence with distinct colored labels.
diagram.imagePrompt: Clean educational schematic diagram of an elementary addition sentence: '3 + 2 = 5' centered on a dark navy background. The plus sign (+) is highlighted inside a bright green glowing circle labeled 'PLUS SIGN'. The equals sign (=) is highlighted inside an amber circle labeled 'EQUALS SIGN'. A soft rounded purple dashed frame encloses the entire equation labeled 'NUMBER SENTENCE'. Minimalist vector line art, clear child-friendly math typography.

concepts.name: Plus Sign (+)
concepts.briefDefinition: A math symbol shaped like a cross that shows numbers are being put together.
concepts.diagramHighlight: The cross-shaped symbol between the numbers 3 and 2

inContext.scenario: You have 3 red apples in a basket, and your friend puts 2 green apples in with them.
inContext.whereToFind: The plus sign (+) is written between 3 and 2 to show you are adding the apples together.

selfCheck.prompt: Which symbol is the plus sign in the number sentence 4 + 1 = 5?
options: The symbol shaped like a cross (+)
selfCheck.hint: Look for the symbol between 4 and 1 that looks like two lines crossing.

concepts.name: Equals Sign (=)
concepts.briefDefinition: A math symbol with two flat bars that shows both sides have the same total amount.
concepts.diagramHighlight: The two parallel horizontal lines between 2 and 5

inContext.scenario: A playground seesaw balances perfectly flat when two small kids sit on one side and one bigger kid sits on the other.
inContext.whereToFind: The equals sign (=) acts like the balance point showing both sides match in value.

selfCheck.prompt: Which symbol is the equals sign in the number sentence 6 + 2 = 8?
options: The symbol with two flat parallel lines (=)
selfCheck.hint: Look for the symbol right before the final answer that has two flat lines stacked on top of each other.

concepts.name: Number Sentence
concepts.briefDefinition: A full row of numbers and symbols that tells a complete math story from start to finish.
concepts.diagramHighlight: The entire line '3 + 2 = 5' enclosed in the dashed box

inContext.scenario: You write down your toy collection: 2 toy cars and 3 toy trucks make 5 vehicles altogether.
inContext.whereToFind: The entire written line '2 + 3 = 5' across your paper is the number sentence.

selfCheck.prompt: Which of these shows a complete number sentence?
selfCheck.hint: Find the choice that shows numbers, a plus sign, and an equals sign all working together.
